I can see a couple of challenges:

  • If a private key ever becomes public, the associated address can be edited at a whim by anyone with that key. Imagine google's server address being swapped with meatspin's, except anyone that has the leaked key can arbitrarily change the address that the associated seed words point to by doing the necessary work.
  • You either have significant data volume issues or significant DDOS risk. If clients must download the blockchain, they have to also download all deltas (communicated by the application or perhaps resolved between peers) before attempting a connection. Alternatively, the block chain could be hosted on a public server, but you would either have to download the entire thing to perform name resolution or else expect unreasonable processing time of the host server to resolve domain name requests.
  • Difficulty may make it prohibitively expensive to make changes to addresses or register new ones as time goes by.
